papers.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
papers.summary: Tested small decision models instead of large chatbots to route API traffic. The setup cut response delay by up to 64% and lowered cloud fees by up to 80%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Edge servers can dispatch incoming user requests faster without paying for expensive large language models.
papers.limitation: Accuracy drops when routing complex requests with more than eight input fields.

papers.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
papers.summary: Evaluated whether AI video generators can show hands completing step-by-step tasks. Current models frequently skipped necessary intermediate steps and failed realistic physics.
papers.practicalUseCase: Provides a benchmark to verify if video generators follow basic physical laws before training robotic arms.
papers.limitation: Current video models still cannot maintain consistent physical contact when handling multiple moving objects.

papers.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
papers.summary: Compressed long chat histories into compact memory vectors that adapt to user preferences. The model recalled past facts accurately across 128,000 words of conversation.
papers.practicalUseCase: Personal AI assistants remember user instructions across weeks of conversation without ballooning token costs.
papers.limitation: Requires fine-tuning the base language model with custom reward signals during training.

papers.title: Video Generation Models: A Survey of Post-Training and Alignment
papers.summary: Surveyed post-training methods used to align video generators with human preferences. The review catalogs reward models and safety filters across current diffusion architectures.
papers.practicalUseCase: Gives AI teams a roadmap for fine-tuning open-source video models to reduce motion artifacts and distortion.
papers.limitation: Review covers existing research literature rather than introducing a new standalone training algorithm.

papers.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
papers.summary: Introduced a calibrated control system that dials personality traits up or down inside language models. Users can request exact levels of friendliness or formality without prompt engineering.
papers.practicalUseCase: Customer service chatbots can maintain an exact corporate tone across conversations without prompt drift.
papers.limitation: Extreme trait values can distort normal language fluency and factual reasoning.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Investigated how dedicated sustainability committees affect green lending in dual banking systems. Banks with formal oversight boards funded significantly more environmental initiatives.
papers.practicalUseCase: Helps banking regulators draft governance guidelines that encourage green project financing.
papers.limitation: Evaluated emerging market banks where sustainability reporting standards vary widely between institutions.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Analyzed global issuance data for sustainability sukuk (Islamic green bonds). Strong legal protections and transparent green frameworks were the main drivers of market adoption.
papers.practicalUseCase: Guides debt issuers on structuring compliant green instruments that attract institutional investors.
papers.limitation: Sample size was limited by the relatively recent history of sustainability sukuk in international debt markets.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Examined how AI and data analytics improve operational speed and credit scoring in Islamic banking. Adopting predictive analytics directly boosted sustainable asset growth.
papers.practicalUseCase: Provides a roadmap for financial institutions to automate credit reviews while honoring Sharia profit-sharing rules.
papers.limitation: Based on data from Jordanian commercial banks; results may differ in non-dual banking environments.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.summary: Studied 218 banks across 12 countries over 13 years to measure how tech adoption affects growth. Digital infrastructure expanded bank assets faster when backed by strong governance.
papers.practicalUseCase: Encourages financial ministries to invest in telecommunication networks to accelerate banking expansion.
papers.limitation: Relies on country-level institutional indicators that may overlook regional differences within nations.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.summary: Compared banking access drivers across Muslim-majority nations and developed OECD economies. Digital payment tools reduced exclusion faster than physical bank branch density.
papers.practicalUseCase: Advises policymakers to prioritize mobile payment rollouts over building brick-and-mortar branches in underserved areas.
papers.limitation: Cross-sectional data cannot prove whether mobile app adoption caused the increase in account ownership.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.summary: Synthesized studies worldwide and found that roughly half of students in intense professional training experience impostor syndrome. High self-doubt directly correlated with academic burnout.
papers.practicalUseCase: Training programs can schedule peer-mentoring groups to normalize self-doubt early in difficult careers.
papers.limitation: Analyzed self-reported questionnaire data that may vary across different regional academic cultures.

papers.title: Positive mood enhances accessibility of unrelated concepts in the first language but not in the foreign language
papers.summary: Tested how positive emotions affect creative thinking when working in native versus foreign languages. A good mood stimulated associative ideas in a mother tongue, but not in a second language.
papers.practicalUseCase: Brainstorming sessions produce more creative ideas when participants can converse in their native language.
papers.limitation: Conducted in a controlled laboratory setting with Polish-English bilingual college participants.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.summary: Validated a standard questionnaire measuring how smartphone and social app use affects mental health and daily focus. The scale separated mindful device habits from compulsive screen time.
papers.practicalUseCase: Workplace wellness apps can use this verified scale to measure digital distraction and screen fatigue.
papers.limitation: Surveyed university students and young professionals; older working populations were not assessed.

papers.title: Organizational debt—Roadblock to agility in software engineering: Exploring an emerging concept and future research for software excellence
papers.summary: Examined how outdated team hierarchies and messy communication slow down software delivery just like bad code.
papers.practicalUseCase: Shows teams how to prune unnecessary approval layers instead of blaming slow progress solely on technical debt.
papers.limitation: Based on qualitative survey interviews across 34 software teams, without automated git metrics.

papers.title: Stress appraisal in the workplace and its associations with productivity and mood: Insights from a multimodal machine learning analysis
papers.summary: Used wearable sensors and machine learning to find that treating workplace challenges as opportunities cut fatigue by 26%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Offers evidence for training employees on cognitive reframing rather than simply cutting task volume.
papers.limitation: Participants wore biometric wristbands in controlled office spaces, not unpredictable home environments.
